boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Oxford-campus spaces for studying, making, writing, meeting, and getting outside, each supported by a current Miami University source.

cards.title: King Library
cards.subtitle: 151 S. Campus Ave. · Oxford campus
cards.notes: Use the library as a starting point for a study session, then choose its reading rooms, reservable rooms, technology, or an on-site support space.
cards.short_summary: Miami’s flagship library combines collections with reservable study rooms, computing, and student-focused services.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami identifies King Library as its flagship library and lists study rooms, computer labs, technology checkout, the MakerSpace, Sidley Lounge, and Howe Writing Center.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current access information and reserve a study room online when needed.

cards.title: King Library MakerSpace
cards.subtitle: Inside King Library · Oxford campus
cards.notes: Plan a hands-on work session here when a project needs making or media equipment; confirm available tools and any required reservation before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A named King Library venue for creation alongside the library’s study and technology services.
cards.evidence_claim: King Library’s official page lists the MakerSpace among its services and popular venues.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s MakerSpace information for current equipment and use procedures.

cards.title: Sidley Lounge
cards.subtitle: Inside King Library · Oxford campus
cards.notes: Meet a classmate or take a break within King Library, then keep the rest of the visit flexible around nearby study rooms and library services.
cards.short_summary: A named lounge within Miami’s flagship library.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami University Libraries names Sidley Lounge as one of King Library’s popular venues.
cards.access_notes: Located within King Library; follow current library building access guidance.

cards.title: Howe Writing Center
cards.subtitle: King Library · 151 S. Campus Ave.
cards.notes: Bring a draft, outline, or writing question to a consultation; use the center’s appointment options to connect with a trained student consultant.
cards.short_summary: A King Library writing-support destination for Miami writers across disciplines.
cards.evidence_claim: The Howe Writing Center says its trained consultants support undergraduate, graduate, and faculty writers and lists its King Library location.
cards.source_title: Howe Writing Center Undergraduate, Graduate and Faculty Writing Support
cards.access_notes: Use the center’s scheduling platform to arrange a consultation.

cards.title: Armstrong Student Center
cards.subtitle: 550 E. Spring St. · Oxford campus
cards.notes: Use this central building to meet, study, find student-engagement offices, or attend scheduled programs; check the building calendar before making plans.
cards.short_summary: Miami’s college union provides meeting, lounge, study, dining, organization, and event space.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami describes Armstrong Student Center as the college union with meeting rooms, quiet study spaces, lounge space, student-organization offices, and event spaces.
cards.source_title: About the Armstrong Student Center | Miami University
cards.access_notes: Current academic-semester building hours are posted by Armstrong Student Center; event spaces may be scheduled.

cards.title: Armstrong Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Armstrong Student Center · Oxford campus
cards.notes: Reserve a room for quiet work or a group project rather than relying on open seating; schedule around the daily time limits shown in the reservation guidance.
cards.short_summary: No-cost study rooms in the student center for current Miami students.
cards.evidence_claim: Armstrong states that current Miami students may use its study rooms at no cost for quiet study and group projects.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through Miami Libraries; the library guidance limits individual and group reservations to two hours per day.

cards.title: Shade Family Room
cards.subtitle: Armstrong Student Center main entrance
cards.notes: Use this room as an easy first stop inside Armstrong, especially when meeting someone or orienting yourself before moving to another part of the center.
cards.short_summary: The named main-entry room that welcomes students and guests into Armstrong Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami identifies the Shade Family Room, formerly Rowan Hall, as the main entrance to Armstrong Student Center on Spring Street.
cards.access_notes: Visit the Armstrong information desk outside the room for a campus map and building information.

cards.title: Richard & Emily Smucker Wiikiaami Room
cards.subtitle: Armstrong Student Center · Oxford campus
cards.notes: Consider this circular room for discussion-oriented programming when it is scheduled or available; treat its Miami Nation–informed design with care and context.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive Armstrong room designed for formal and spontaneous discussion-oriented programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami says the Wiikiaami Room honors Miami Nation heritage and has seating suited to scheduled and spontaneous discussion-oriented programming.
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on programming and scheduling within Armstrong Student Center.

cards.title: Silvoor Biological Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: 910 Silvoor Lane · Oxford
cards.notes: Take a casual spring walk through the sanctuary and its wildflower garden, using the official trail information to plan a respectful outdoor visit.
cards.short_summary: A 2.5-acre Miami natural-area sanctuary with a wildflower garden and trail access.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami describes Silvoor Biological Sanctuary as a 2.5-acre tract with an extensive wildflower garden and gives its entrance at 910 Silvoor Lane.
cards.source_title: Places to Visit | Miami University Natural Areas
cards.access_notes: Use the official Silvoor Trail Map and remain on designated routes.

cards.title: College Woods
cards.subtitle: Miami University Natural Areas · Oxford
cards.notes: Choose the loop for a short outdoor reset, and use the official trail map to stay on route while observing the woodland rather than disturbing it.
cards.short_summary: A 16-acre second-growth woodlot in Miami’s natural-area system.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami identifies College Woods as a 16-acre second-growth woodlot and provides a College Woods Trail Map.
cards.source_title: Places to Visit | Miami University Natural Areas
cards.access_notes: Consult the official College Woods Trail Map before visiting and follow posted trail guidance.
